summary_use_case_description: Velox runs real-time personalization and reranking for a high-traffic ecommerce site. Primary goal: deterministic latency at peak traffic (flash sales) and predictable per-token cost. Looking to evaluate Redwood Dedicated for reserved GPU capacity with autoscaling that preserves SLOs without excessive cost.

CTO quote: "cannot tolerate more than 2% tail-latency spikes during Holiday launches". Interested in warm pools & fast scale-up for 10x traffic surges. technical_requirements: Throughput: sustained 500 requests/sec (avg 30 tokens/request) with headroom for 2x burst
Latency SLO: p95 < 120ms for recommendation endpoint; p99 < 300ms acceptable for short periods
Tail tolerance: <2% spikes beyond SLO during 1-hour peak windows
Availability: 99.95% monthly for dedicated pool; prefer financial credit clause for missed throughput SLA
Data residency: EU for EU customers, must support regional routing
reserved_gpu_plan: Initial proposal: 4x NVIDIA A100 (40GB) reserved with option to bump to 8x for peak season. Plan includes a baseline warm pool of 8 workers per GPU type (80 warm processes), ability to burst to shared capacity. Billing model: monthly reserved+burst credits. Customer requests an example: 4x reserved should guarantee minimum throughput of 350 req/s (30 tok/req) and capacity to absorb 2x bursts via pre-warmed workers.
autoscaling_policies: Scale-up: add 1 GPU-equivalent worker within 20s when queue depth > 50 or GPU util > 70% for 30s. Aggressive pre-warm on predicted traffic (time-based schedule for sales). Scale-down: safe window 10 minutes of sustained util < 25% and cold-cache eviction permitted only when warm-pool > configured minimum. Customer emphasis: must avoid killing warm KV caches during scale-down for at least 15 minutes after scale event.
warm_pool_strategy: Maintain warm pool sized at 20% of baseline traffic (~8 warm workers) with fast-start provisioning. Warm pools must retain KV cache for pinned model variants for 15 minutes after last use. Pre-warm triggers: scheduled events (marketing calendar), predictive signals from traffic model, manual ramp for A/B canary. Desire for APIs to pin warm workers to tenant to avoid cold starts.
queueing_behavior: Allow soft-queue up to 500ms per request under burst; backpressure policy: degrade non-critical reranking calls first, route lower-priority traffic to hosted fallback. SLA requires queueing not to increase p95 latency beyond 120ms for high-priority requests. Observability: token-level queue time, per-route queue depth metrics in Console.
sla_negotiation_points: Throughput guarantees (min req/sec per reserved GPU)
Definitions: what counts as a missed throughput window (5m/15m) and remediation credits
Warm-start guarantees & penalties if warm pools not available during scheduled events
Scale-down cooldown windows and cache retention guarantees
Regional failover latency caps and cross-region fallback costs
